driveStages.driveBoundary: Freely backdrivable massless/unforced input in actual contact; prescribed-height bench holds the drive input and retains its coupled inertia.

alpha20SuPermission: Owner approved Su geometry adjustment, while explicitly retaining the spring rate and reference preload.

alpha20RejectedTwoVariableCandidate.search: Bounded coarse horn1..301mm/Sv−300..900mm plus targeted refinement and local multistart; not an infeasibility proof.

rejectedRestoringStudy.rejection: Strong K1173 tune gave downward equivalent assist near extension and both prescribed-height runs reached travel limits near1.98s. Of three upward-assist candidates, two ran the prescribed bench but none avoided terrain endstops. No restoring trial is saved as a final design. Exact final benchmark outcomes belong to the separate paired-engine report.

massBasis.wheelTreatment: With fixed world wheel height and zero contact moment, wheel gravity has zero stance work. Its weight remains in the ground reaction and in dynamic wheel mass/inertia. Moving link/compound gravity is included at each actual COM; alpha changes its world-height work.

fits.method: Bounded sampled minimax geometry fit followed by a horn-only root of static holding torque at135deg. This balances the saved ride pose; it is not a height controller or terrain stability guarantee.

limits: Supported-stance gravity compensation only. Both saved designs balance the135deg ride pose and retain upward spring-equivalent assist, but near-neutral support is not passive world-height regulation. Geometry-only trials did not solve the150mm terrain case without other failures; no hidden motor bias, damping or changes to k/preload are used. At alpha20 finite-link COM gravity makes the equivalent support target pose-dependent. Working stops are inset from the singular ideal90-degree endpoint. Prescribed-height bench requires explicit10mm transition; contact requires0. Entered250/300Nm commands are illustrative ideal joint torques, not certified actuator capability. Actual outcomes, impact losses, packaging and strength require separate validation.
